title: Vragen stellen — inversie en vraagwoorden
summary: Yes/no questions by inversion, the dropped -t with jij, and the question words

blocks.title: Yes/no questions: just swap
blocks.body: To ask a yes/no question, put the **verb first** and the subject behind it. That's it — no extra 'do' like English. *Jij werkt* (you work) → *Werk jij?* (do you work?). Statement, flip the first two, done.

blocks.title: The -t drop: Werk jij?, not Werkt jij?
blocks.body: Here's the twist. When *jij* (or *je*) comes **right after** the verb, the verb **loses its -t** and goes back to the bare stem. *Jij werkt* → *Werk jij?* This happens only with *jij/je*, and only when it sits behind the verb.
blocks.callout: *hij* keeps its -t: *Werkt hij?* Only *jij/je* triggers the drop.

blocks.prompt: Turn 'Jij begint om negen uur' into a question.
blocks.explain: Verb first, and because *jij* follows it, drop the -t: *Begin jij om negen uur?*

blocks.title: Question words
blocks.body: For open questions, start with a **question word**, then the verb, then the subject — the verb still lands in slot 2, exactly like yesterday's fronting. The question word is your front element.

blocks.prompt: You want to ask where someone lives. Which word do you start with?
blocks.explain: *waar* = where. *wanneer* is when, *waarom* is why — easy to mix up, so drill them.

blocks.prompt: Ask 'What are you doing today?' — use jij. (verb: doen → doe)
blocks.hint: Question word, then verb, then jij — mind the -t drop.
blocks.explain: *Wat doe jij vandaag?* Question word in slot 1, verb in slot 2, and *doen* loses its -t behind *jij*.

blocks.scene: Daan is nosy about your new routine at the café

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.spotlight: Question word + verb + jij — and *werk*, not 'werkt'.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ik werk in de Pijp. Bij een klein bureau.
lines.en: I work in de Pijp. At a small agency.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.nl: Leuk! En hoe laat begin je?
lines.en: Nice! And what time do you start?
lines.spotlight: *hoe laat* = what time; *begin je* drops the -t too.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.en: Do you work on Friday too?
lines.spotlight: A yes/no question: verb first, *je* behind it.

questions.q: What time does the learner usually start work?
Which day does Daan ask about?

blocks.prompt: Write four questions you'd ask a new Dutch colleague — one yes/no question and three with different question words. Watch the -t drop after jij/je.
